q.t: All living beings are made of…
q.e: A cell is to an organism what a brick is to a wall.

q.t: Who first described 'cells' in cork (1665)?
q.e: In his book Micrographia.

q.t: Who is the Father of Microbiology?
q.e: First to see and describe bacteria and blood cells.

q.t: Which part controls the cell's activities?
q.e: The cell's control room.

q.t: Which part is found in plant cells but not animal cells?
q.e: Plants also have chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

q.t: Chloroplasts contain…
q.e: They make food by photosynthesis.

q.t: Living things too small to see with the naked eye are…
q.e: Also called microbes.

q.t: Yeast is a…
q.e: A unicellular fungus.

q.t: Lactobacillus turns milk into…
q.e: It makes lactic acid.

q.t: Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of…
q.e: Beans, peas, lentils.

q.t: Why are cells stained before viewing?
q.e: Cells are nearly transparent.

q.t: Why is glycerin added to the slide?
o: Stops cells drying and clears the image
q.e: It keeps the specimen moist.

q.t: Why lower the coverslip at an angle?
q.e: Bubbles look like dark circles and hide the cells.

q.t: Onion peel cells look…
o: Nearly rectangular, packed with no gaps
q.e: The cell wall gives them a firm shape.

q.t: Cheek cells look…
q.e: Thin and flat — a protective lining.

q.t: Nerve cells are long and branched to…
o: Carry messages quickly to distant parts
q.e: Shape follows function.

q.t: Bacteria differ from all other groups because they have…
q.e: Genetic material sits loose in the nucleoid.

q.t: Viruses are…
o: Acellular and multiply only inside living cells
q.e: They aren't made of cells.

q.t: Biogas is mostly…
q.e: Made by microbes decomposing waste without oxygen.

q.t: Microalgae release how much of Earth's oxygen?
q.e: They photosynthesise in water, soil and air.

q.t: Why does dough with yeast rise?
q.e: The gas makes the dough fluffy.

q.t: Why add warm water, not cold, to yeast dough?
q.e: Cold slows yeast right down.

q.t: Why doesn't curd set in cold milk in a fridge?
o: Lactobacillus grows well only in warmth
q.e: Bacteria multiply slowly in cold.

q.t: Yeast makes ___; Lactobacillus makes ___.
q.e: Both are fermentation with different products.

q.t: Why do farmers grow legumes in rotation with other crops?
o: Rhizobium adds usable nitrogen to the soil
q.e: The leftover nitrogen enriches soil for the next crop.

q.t: Plants can't use nitrogen gas directly. Rhizobium…
o: Converts it into a usable form
q.e: That's nitrogen fixation.

q.t: Why don't microbes spoil pickles and murabbas?
o: High salt or sugar stops their growth
q.e: Salt and sugar act as preservatives.

q.t: Peels buried under soil for weeks become manure because…
o: Microbes decompose them into simpler nutrients
q.e: Decomposition returns nutrients to the soil.

q.t: Levels of organisation from small to large:
o: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
q.e: Similar cells make tissues; tissues make organs…

q.t: The largest known single cell is…
o: The yolk of an ostrich egg
q.e: 130–170 mm across.

q.t: Three differences between plant and animal cells:
q.e: Plants have all three; animals lack them or have tiny vacuoles.

q.t: Without decomposers, what would happen?
o: Dead matter would pile up and nutrients never return
q.e: Decomposition makes the nutrient cycle a cycle.

q.t: Why is a bean farmer less in need of nitrogen fertiliser than a wheat farmer?
o: Rhizobium in bean roots fixes nitrogen
q.e: Legumes partner with nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

q.t: What advantage do multicellular organisms have?
o: Specialised cells each do one job well
q.e: One cell must do every job; many cells can specialise.

q.t: Ananda Mohan Chakrabarty developed a bacterium that…
q.e: Patented in 1980.

q.t: An electron microscope magnifies about…
q.e: Revealing structures an ordinary microscope can't.

q.t: Which is unicellular?
q.e: Bacteria, Amoeba, Paramecium, yeast are unicellular.

q.t: Which microbe group contains chlorophyll?
q.e: Algae make their own food.

q.t: Spirulina is called a superfood because it…
o: Is over 60% protein with vitamin B12
q.e: Very little fat or sugar.

q.t: Ancient Indian texts called tiny entities…
q.e: Both Drishya (visible) and Adrishya (invisible).
